text: Spent half a day today window shopping for a dishwasher at nearby retail stores with D. Do I have the money to pay for a dishwasher? Perhaps, No. I can’t splurge money on such things. Spending 40K on a dishwasher is a pointless affair. Instead spend it on learning a new skill that will give a better job.

Started with those email conversations again, with BNR. I could just focus on more important things - finding a software developer job. Had a good sleep in the afternoon having eaten a sumptuous meal with Ragi balls, chicken curry and Jira rice. AK didn’t show up for the class this evening possibly because of tomorrow’s exam.

Spent the morning and a little bit of the afternoon assembling the exercise bike that G had recently bought. My back and hands are aching after the chore. Now at 6.10 PM, I am waiting Ak to join the session for Maths tutoring. Wonder if he’s going to turn up. A waste of my time, simply waiting. I have started watching this new TV series called Moonbase 8 on Voot streaming app. It seems I will spend a lot of time watching it over the next week or so. Finished watching Larry David’s ’Curb your enthusiasm’ complete series. My PSN membership will end today or tomorrow. Had spent enough time playing RDR2 online. Another time killer but sometimes pleasurable. I’m lagging behind with my studies - Algorithms CLRS, programming tasks and others. Wonder if I’ll make enough time for those.

More - ask for more. More money, more food, more happiness, more this and more that. A sense of contentment prevails as I sit through the time. Passing of time, chirpings of the bird, rustling of leaves, clickety sound of the keyboard, sleepy as I feel laid in the chair. The aroma of the cooking breakfast hits my nose as I feel the urge to go down and eat it. I have been enjoying life to the fullest through relaxation and entertainment. The toil of work beckons me only when the world expects me to toil for a greater purpose - for survival, blah and blah.

I had to move the ’Money Plant’ from the window grill inside my room to the balcony outside. Reason being: “According to Vastu, I shouldn’t grow a creeper inside the room”, as V says. “It denotes dependence on parents for everything - food, shelter, emotional support, financial support blah blah”. Now, since I have moved it out of the room to the balcony, I will become independent - both emotionally and financially. I do crave for independence and wouldn’t mind doing a silly thing such as moving the plant from one place to another. As if it would magically get me to independence. These are the kind of reasons I need to provide myself for the things I’m facing and the need to meet the aspirations that I secretly nurture. The aspiration of being independent, have enough money to sustain a living on my own as a free individual.

Time for Alain Du Botton’s philosophical meditation. I will get my white covered notebook (with custom stickers on it) and start using it for jotting down my anxieties, qualms and ambitions. Later, I am going to start looking at the work that needs attention. I wonder why do I frequently fluctuate between ’All or Nothing’ sort of thinking and its associated actions.

After reading (or at least parts of) the book ’How to be Idle?’ by Tom Hodgkinson, I have started to embrace the anti-work culture. The same anti-work culture that’s part of the SubReddit post. ’The Great Resignation’ is another phenomenon associated with this Reddit post. The eternal question that I have always and most often am confronted with is - “Why should I work for someone else for the sake of earning money?”, “Why can’t I build something of my own, be self-sufficient, self-reliant, and so on with what I have with me already?”, “Why is there is this eternal need to satisfy every desire that I have through money?”, “How can I be more frugal in my spending and usage of resources?”. I wish I were writing all these on paper, instead of using electricity. Power to run a complex computer and the LCD display consuming that power. Isn’t it a wastage? Paper and ink are more economical I’d say. Even if electricity were free of cost, should I be using it?

A long discussion in the morning with D and G over work, job, employment, income and so on. A boring exercise - this work, trying to get payment and using that to buy things. An everlasting endurance of my faculties to wander and find work.

After a lavish extended weekend, I still feel I haven’t gotten enough. Enough of what’s due to me: luxury, pleasure, adventure, sleep, relaxation and enlightenment. Lay down, shut down, don’t wake up. What is waking life? Life without the sleep or life without life? Decipher the mundane, the boring: embrace boredom. Despising boredom is a tragedy. Sit back, enjoy the show, dance and deuce.
